title: Positive scalar resonators obey moment constraints that matrix coupling can escape
statement: In the source B=1 energy normalization, for fixed scalar-envelope/static-hop class at E0=3/2 let alpha=-L1>0,beta=-L2>0. A finite positive scalar-pole family with dj=Omega_j-E0!=0 and q1=q2=0 obeys M2=sum rj/dj^2=gamma*alpha-1>0 and M3=sum rj/dj^3=gamma*beta/2. If alpha<=beta/4, at least one pole has E0<Omega_j<2. Also q3>=gamma*L3+3*gamma^2*beta^2/[2*(gamma*alpha-1)]>gamma*(L3+3*beta^2/(2*alpha)); a nonnegative final bracket forces q3>0.

Exact derivative premises alpha>0,beta>0 and M2>0; upper-band result additionally alpha<=beta/4, third-jet obstruction additionally L3+3*beta^2/(2*alpha)>=0.

body: If all poles avoid the upper in-band interval, dj<0 or dj>=1/2 and termwise dj^-2>=(1/2)*dj^-3. Thus M2>=M3/2 implies alpha-beta/4>=1/gamma>0, contradicting alpha<=beta/4. Cauchy-Schwarz on sqrt(rj)/dj and sqrt(rj)/dj^2 gives M3^2<=M2*M4; substituting the required moments into q3=gamma*L3+6*M4 proves the lower bound. Finite sums are the accepted scope; infinite families need convergent moments and justified differentiation.
